comparisons.peer_topic: Hyperscale Customer Base and Product Applications
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's data center products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, and adaptive SOCs, are purchased by large public cloud providers and hyperscale private data centers. These customers incorporate the products into servers for web applications, public cloud services, and AI workloads such as generative AI models.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD describe how their products are utilized by infrastructure providers (telecom operators for AVGO, cloud providers for AMD) to run modern applications and services. AVGO's Telco Cloud Platform helps telecom operators 'create monetizable services'. AMD's data center products are purchased by 'public cloud service providers' who 'incorporate the products into servers... to operate web-based applications or to support public cloud computing and storage service offerings, including... AI workloads'. Both disclosures highlight the role of their respective technologies in enabling service delivery at the infrastructure level.

sentences.text: • Telco Cloud Platform: This solution supports network operations for telecom operators and communications service providers to modernize their infrastructure and allows them to create monetizable services. The modernization of the telecom infrastructure is critical to enabling operational agility, onboarding and delivering services much faster across domains and simplifying operations with automation.

Hyperscale data centers use these products to operate web-based applications or to support public cloud computing and storage service offerings, including but not limited to AI workloads such as generative AI models.

comparisons.peer_topic: x86 Ecosystem Strategy and Advisory Group
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's core strategy relies on the x86 ecosystem, advancing it through microarchitectures focused on performance and efficiency. In 2024, the company created an advisory group to expand ecosystem compatibility, simplify software development, and identify future architectural needs.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Intel discuss their strategic positioning in the broader computing and network infrastructure ecosystem, though through different architectural lenses. AVGO focuses on its Telco Cloud Platform specifically for telecom operators to 'modernize their infrastructure'. Intel discusses its core 'x86 ecosystem' strategy which provides 'end-to-end solutions, scaling from data center to network' and 'edge computing'. While AVGO targets the specific 'Telco' vertical with a cloud platform, Intel targets the fundamental x86 architecture across multiple infrastructure layers including network and edge, aiming to 'expand ecosystem compatibility' and 'simplify software development'.

sentences.text: • Telco Cloud Platform: This solution supports network operations for telecom operators and communications service providers to modernize their infrastructure and allows them to create monetizable services. The modernization of the telecom infrastructure is critical to enabling operational agility, onboarding and delivering services much faster across domains and simplifying operations with automation.

Our product offerings provide end-to-end solutions, scaling from data center to network, PCs, edge computing, and the emerging fields of AI and autonomous driving, to serve an increasingly smart and connected world.

In 2024, we announced the creation of an advisory group to expand the x86 ecosystem by enabling compatibility across platforms, simplifying software development, and providing developers with a platform to identify architectural needs and features to create innovative and scalable solutions for the future.

comparisons.peer_summary: Industrial memory demand is fueled by the adoption of IoT devices, manufacturing automation, machine-to-machine communication, transportation, surveillance, retail, and smart infrastructure, requiring reliable and high-performance memory solutions.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Micron identify 'smart infrastructure' and modernized operational environments as key drivers for their respective offerings. AVGO's Telco Cloud Platform is designed to help telecom operators 'modernize their infrastructure' and 'simplify operations'. Micron notes that 'Industrial memory demand is being fueled by the increasing adoption of IoT devices... and smart infrastructure'. Both disclosures link their products to the broader trend of upgrading and connecting infrastructure, with AVGO providing the cloud/platform layer and Micron providing the memory components for such environments.

comparisons.peer_summary: In fiscal year 2024, the company launched NVIDIA DGX Cloud, an AI-training-as-a-service platform with cloud infrastructure, pretrained models, and expert access, hosted in partnership with leading cloud service providers.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVIDIA are launching specific cloud-based platform services to enable infrastructure modernization and service delivery, moving beyond pure hardware/software sales to managed or hosted platforms. AVGO's Telco Cloud Platform supports telecom operators to 'modernize their infrastructure' and 'simplify operations with automation' for monetizable services. Similarly, NVIDIA launched 'NVIDIA DGX Cloud, an AI-training-as-a-service platform' which provides 'cloud-based infrastructure and software for AI' and is 'hosted in partnership with leading cloud service providers' to deliver these capabilities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Innovation impact on wireless communications and customer value
comparisons.peer_summary: Innovations developed and integrated into the product portfolio aim to expand wireless communications opportunities, enhance product value, and enable customers to improve service performance, offer services more affordably, and introduce revenue-generating broadband data services ahead of competition.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Qualcomm frame their infrastructure solutions around enabling customers to improve performance and value in their communications services. AVGO states that the Telco Cloud Platform allows telecom operators to 'create monetizable services' and 'enable operational agility'. Qualcomm similarly states that its innovations are expected to 'enable our customers to improve the performance or value of their existing services, offer these services more affordably and introduce revenue-generating broadband data services'. Both disclosures focus on the business outcome for the telecom/communications operator regarding service monetization and performance.

The modernization of the telecom infrastructure is critical to enabling operational agility, onboarding and delivering services much faster across domains and simplifying operations with automation.

These innovations are expected to enable our customers to improve the performance or value of their existing services, offer these services more affordably and introduce revenue-generating broadband data services ahead of their competition.
